liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review): Phil plays the song to the point of no return, as if knocking off loose rocks [28]
- Phil played large, resonant bass chords during the tuning and the song's beginning [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-07-27.sbd.clemens.78746.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 131 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Initial hiss clears up by the end of Jack Straw, improving overall audio quality; Soundboard recordings from this run are described as less than par in quality; The entire song is spent adjusting levels of different instruments in the mix [19][21][23]
- **gd1982-07-27.mtx.sirmick.109780.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 135 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Charlie Miller's mastering makes Jerry louder and fixes issues in Jack Straw and Other One; The audience is louder than preferred, though the overall recording is still considered good [24]
- **gd1982-07-27.167100.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.sclugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 137 min [4]
- **gd1982-07-27.156435.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 135 min [6]
- **gd1982-07-27.naks.mason.129411.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [11]. Said about its sound: The sound quality starts to improve noticeably around the time of this song [28]
- **gd1982-07-27.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102570.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 135 min; rated 2.4/5 by 5 [12]. Said about its sound: The recording features top-notch clarity and fidelity, with close-in crowd whooping [27]

## Around the show

- Rainy weather created an intimate atmosphere, leading fans to name the run "Wet Rocks" [17]
- The reviewer was twenty, attending their first Grateful Dead concert while in Boulder for Kerouac's anniversary [26]
- The reviewer drove Allen Ginsberg in a rental car to a radio interview in Boulder [26]
- The second set is considered among the finest Grateful Dead music from any era [17]
- The performance ranks in the top three of all Grateful Dead history for the reviewer [18]
- The reviewer considers the July 29th show the best of the three Red Rocks performances [20]
- The setlist suggests this show was a warm-up for the superior final night of the run [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-07-27.sbd.clemens.78746.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jake Clemens; source: SBD>Cass/1>DAT [1]
- **gd1982-07-27.mtx.sirmick.109780.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Matrix 60% soundboard/40% audience; sources: 1 - SBD>Cass/1>DAT>HD-P2>Soundforge 6.0>Flac Frontend>FLAC (shnid 78746) Tranfer by Jake Clemens 2 - (FOB)… [2]. Also: The matrix combines a soundboard with crisp vocals and an audience recording with better highs; Dave from Sugarmegs suggested the project, and the two sources complement each other well [2]
- **gd1982-07-27.167100.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.sclugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [4]. Also: A Beyer M160 and Sennheiser 421 blend supplies a thirteen-second patch in The Wheel [4]
- **gd1982-07-27.156435.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M88 mics > Unknown deck > Jim Vita's 1st generation cassettes (Maxell MX-90) [6]. Also: Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies On The Road Again and most of Roses [6]
- **gd1982-07-27.naks.mason.129411.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: flac16 ; Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes; Senn 441's>Sony D5>Mason's Nak 550: Transferred on Mason's restored Nak550… [11]. Also: The reviewer thanks Mason for his hard work taping the show, noting he has passed away [28]
- **gd1982-07-27.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102570.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [12]. Also: Jim Wise recorded the show with a handheld microphone, likely two-thirds back from the stage [27]

Jim Wise recorded the show with a handheld microphone, likely two-thirds back from the stage
The recording features top-notch clarity and fidelity, with close-in crowd whooping
The show is considered solidly played but average, elevated by the stellar recording quality
The sound quality starts to improve noticeably around the time of this song
Phil plays the song to the point of no return, as if knocking off loose rocks
The reviewer thanks Mason for his hard work taping the show, noting he has passed away
The matrix combines a soundboard with crisp vocals and an audience recording with better highs
Dave from Sugarmegs suggested the project, and the two sources complement each other well
Scott Wiseman provided source cassettes, and Charlie Miller coordinated the transfer effort
A Beyer M160 and Sennheiser 421 blend supplies a thirteen-second patch in The Wheel
Jim Vita provided first-generation cassettes, and Charlie Miller handled the transfer and coordination
Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies On The Road Again and most of Roses
Doug Lamarre's Nakamichi 300 source supplies a forty-seven-second patch in the Drums section
